head: Gateway Gaston: what they want, what they hate, how they feel about us
about: Gateway Gaston connects people in Gaston County, North Carolina to local help, fast and with dignity. Its new project, Journey Home, is for neighbors who have no home. Client since 17 Sep 2026. Contact: Dwayne Burks, who leads Gateway Gaston and records his own videos on iPhone. Our lead: Atdhe.

loves: Dignity. People are neighbors, not cases.
One clear ask in every video. Comment “I'm in” or send a message.
The Journey Home logo swishing in with sound at the end.
Honest feedback. He wants to be told what is not best practice.
hates: Pixelated faces. DV survivors must stay anonymous in a tasteful way, never pixelation.
Posts with no clear ask. People watch and do nothing.
His own bad background in the first videos.
Long videos. He stops watching past about 30 seconds.
The story told a different way each time.
how_to_cut: Hook at 0:00 on his strongest line. The logo comes only at the end.
Keep his words. Do not add facts, numbers or new words.
One ask per video, shown as text: Comment “I'm in”.
Captions on the whole time. Most people watch with the sound off.
DV survivors: anonymous through framing, silhouette or voice. Never pixelation.
No added stock footage. Use what he sent.
If a file is not good enough, write it on the item. Do not fix it in secret.

## Key Contacts
- **Dwayne Burks** — leads / represents Gateway Gaston. `dwayne@gatewaygaston.org`.
- **William** — Gateway Gaston staff/volunteer; Dwayne is to confirm with him whether 3–4 videos in one month are feasible, then schedule his Zoom interviews with Atdhe.

## 🎯 Goals & Preferences
- **Org:** Gateway Gaston, `gatewaygaston.org` — Gaston County, NC (~225k population). Coordinates benevolent care via a maintained resource database and a rapid-response callback promise (within 90 minutes) to connect people to services **with dignity**.
- **Operating context:** highly fragmented / siloed agencies across the county; the Salvation Army shelter closure left the county with **no homeless shelter**.
- **Structure:** largely volunteer-run. One part-time remote staffer in TX handles callbacks. An intern is producing 8–12 short videos for a separate education/communication tool (**Real Life and Logic**).
- **Existing content:** some website video explainers; a raw-audio podcast *"What It's Really Like to Be Unhoused"* used by a local college. No consistent, strategic video output.
**The two storytelling jobs Dwayne named:**
1. Explain **"how the county got in this mess"** once, consistently, at quality — so Dwayne stops re-giving and re-varying the talk himself.
2. Capture **2027 success stories** to support the 2028 county-wide scale-up.
**Hard creative constraint:** DV survivor stories require **anonymity handled tastefully — explicitly NOT pixelation**. Treat this as a locked client rule, not a preference.
**Stated pain:** no owner for the video/content process; volunteer capacity is the binding constraint; current social has no clear ask/offer, so audience does not convert to donors.
